svg.title: Staging: write where nobody looks, then commit
svg.desc: The staged protocol writes the new tiles under staging/<size>/<root>/, a private name that only this exact tree can have. Then it signs, then compare-and-swaps the lock, then copies the staged tiles into their public paths and publishes the checkpoint. If it crashes after the lock, recovery finds the staged files for the locked size and root and rolls forward. If it crashes before the lock, the staged files belong to a tree nobody committed to, and are simply ignored.

text.tspan: staged files of a tree nobody committed to.
Ignored. The next round stages under another root.
public paths are only ever written with tiles of a committed tree,
so write-once storage never refuses, and nothing beyond the lock is ever public.
Let's Encrypt's MTC tile code has a similar step: Stage under a prefix from size and root, then Publish.
